evals.prompt: evals/files/feedback.txt has customer comments, one per line (imagine there are 300 of them, not 12). Before I read anything, sort them into bug reports, feature requests, billing questions, and praise so I only open the bugs first.
evals.expected_output: The agent sorts the lines programmatically with the classifier service, stating the labels and reporting grouped verdicts rather than JSON.
expectations: The classify skill is invoked from the description alone
The comments are read from the file programmatically and sent as one batch, not one call per line
The labels used are stated in the report, and include a catch-all such as 'none of these' or 'unknown' so each line lands in exactly one
The report groups the comments under their labels instead of showing raw JSON
Results are matched back to the original line order

evals.prompt: Use the classify skill on evals/files/feedback.txt with the labels: bug, feature request, billing question, praise, none of these. This is a dry run: do not send anything, but show the exact request you would make (the command and the body shape) and say what the report would look like.
evals.expected_output: A well-formed batch request: JSON body built by an encoder, passed on standard input, default fast tier, single-label mode.
expectations: The body uses the inputs array and the labels array, and does not mix input, inputs, or items
The body is serialized with a JSON encoder and piped to curl with --data-binary @-, so the comment text is never placed inside the shell command string
The request goes to POST https://classifier.dev with a content-type: application/json header
The tier is fast (or left at its default), and multi is not set
The planned report shows verdicts in the form 'label · confidence' or grouped under labels, not the raw JSON

evals.prompt: Use the classify skill. I wanted to keep only billing-related lines from evals/files/relevance-inputs.txt and drop the rest. The service already answered; its saved response is in evals/files/relevance-response.json (same order as the input lines). Do not call the service again. Apply the filter and report.
evals.expected_output: Only the two negative verdicts with numeric confidence of at least 0.8 are discarded; the weak and unscored ones are kept and flagged.
expectations: Exactly two lines are discarded: the ones with 'not billing related' and confidence 0.91 and 0.88
The line with confidence 0.74 is kept and flagged as a weak verdict
The line with null confidence is kept and reported as unscored
The line with 'billing related' at 0.62 is kept and flagged as weak
The report lists the kept lines and states the discarded count (2)
The agent does not rerun the request or change the labels to get a preferred answer

evals.prompt: Use the classify skill on evals/files/private-notes.txt: label each note as account access, account deletion, app problem, or other. Use the real service if you can.
evals.expected_output: The notes contain credentials and personal data, so nothing is sent; the agent classifies locally and marks the verdicts as its own judgement, or asks for redacted input.
expectations: The text of the notes is not sent to classifier.dev
The agent says why: the text would leave the machine and contains secrets or personal information
The agent either classifies locally against the same labels and marks every verdict as its own judgement, or asks for redacted input
No invented numeric confidence is attached to a locally produced verdict
Credentials and personal details from the file are not repeated in the report

evals.prompt: Use the classify skill on 40 invented one-line support messages about a bike shop, labels: order status, repair booking, complaint, other. Assume the service answers HTTP 503 with an HTML error page both on the first call and on the one retry. Walk through what you do and what you tell me.
evals.expected_output: One retry with backoff, then an honest report of the cause and a clearly marked local fallback.
expectations: The agent retries exactly once with backoff and does not loop
The agent reports the actual cause (HTTP 503, with the request identifier if one was present), not a vague 'it failed'
The fallback is local judgement against the same labels, explicitly marked as the agent's judgement, with no invented confidence
If the items cannot be reviewed locally, the agent says which remain unclassified

evals.prompt: Use the classify skill. For these four invented tickets, give me both a topic (billing, shipping, account, other) and an urgency (low, high) for each: 1) 'I was charged twice and rent is due tomorrow.' 2) 'Can you change the email on my profile?' 3) 'My parcel has not moved in two weeks.' 4) 'What are your opening hours?'. Show the request you would send; do not send it.
evals.expected_output: A dimensions request using items and dimensions, with no top-level labels and no multi-label options.
expectations: The body uses items together with a dimensions object holding topic and urgency label arrays
The body has no top-level labels, no multi, and no max_labels
The planned report reads results per item and per dimension (results[i].dimensions[name])
Confidence is checked for null before any threshold is applied

evals.prompt: Use the classify skill. Sort these 300 support tickets with the labels billing, outage, feature request, and spam, then drop the junk so I only read what matters. The file is tickets.csv.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks which labels count as junk before filtering, keeps everything until answered, and applies the 0.8 confidence rule to the discard side only.
expectations: The agent asks which of the four labels are the discard side (for example spam) instead of assuming
Until the user answers, no item is discarded
Once the discard label is known, only items with that label and numeric confidence of at least 0.8 are discarded; unscored and low-confidence items are kept
A failed request is retried at most once in total

evals.prompt: Here are three error messages from our log: 'disk quota exceeded on /var/data', 'user clicked help button', 'connection reset by peer'. Which one is the most worrying? Just tell me what you think.
evals.expected_output: A handful of items already in context is judged directly; no API call is made.
expectations: The classify skill is not invoked and no request is made to classifier.dev
The agent answers directly from its own judgement

evals.prompt: Go through the open requests on our project's issue tracker, work out which ones are real bugs, decide which are ready for a developer, and write a brief for each ready one.
evals.expected_output: Verifying published requests and writing agent-ready briefs is triage, not bulk labelling.
expectations: The classify skill is not invoked as the main approach
The agent routes the work through triage (categorize, verify, refine, write briefs) with a maintainer decision
